summary: Manual extraction for rakudai-kishi-main vol-19. The volume resumes the Wakaba House crisis after Harima Tendo's reveal. Kanata receives a direct warning from Itsuki Kurogane that the blind old man sheltered by Wakaba House is the escaped terrorist Daien. Toka confronts Tendo at a graveyard, but his Excessively Awakened body cannot be harmed by ordinary attacks and his Device Ame-no-Murakumo unleashes disaster-class lightning, fire, wind, earthquakes and landslides across northern Kyushu. Moroboshi and Jounosaki arrive by teleport to save Toka and Misogi, but Moroboshi judges that he cannot defeat Tendo alone and retreats. Five days later, Kurono briefs elite knights on Awakening, Desperado and Excessive Awakening, planning a joint attack based on World Crisis and Moroboshi's Tiger Bite; Toka, however, is broken by Tendo's gravity, which shows her an inescapable crucifixion-like death whenever she tries to face him. The crisis then expands when the United States Pacific Fleet, led by Douglas Upton, invades Japan's EEZ and claims that Prime Minister Bakuya Tsukikage confessed to League-Rebellion collusion. Itsuki declares a national emergency and recalls Kurono from Kyushu to defend Tokyo, leaving Kyushu to evacuate under Tendo's growing Red Lotus Hell blizzard. Nishikata Hisako and Wakaba House help Toka stop forcing herself into solitary heroism: Nishikata reframes her parents' chamomile wish as permission to live and smile, while the children give Toka chamomile hairpins and remind her that everyone can fight in their own capacity. Toka proposes restoring Kyushu's damaged high-voltage grid and receiving all available electricity at Central Substation. Itsuki initially refuses the civilian risk but authorizes the plan after Toka explains that she cannot win alone and instead trusts everyone to lend her power. In Tokyo, Oreki, Renren, Ikazuchi, Kirihara, Kagami and Kurono hold the capital's first defense line, but Upton's flying Device Enterprise pins Kurono offshore and prevents a quick return to Kyushu. In Fukuoka, Moroboshi recruits Kuraudo as the second arrow, enchants Orochimaru with Tiger Bite to create Gluttonous Serpent, and lets Kuraudo carve through Tendo's storm defenses. Moroboshi then pierces Tendo with Musou Ittetsu, devouring his soul; Tendo nevertheless persists as a fading will in his disaster magic and tries to force Moroboshi into solitary Awakening with twelve giant Ame-no-Murakumo blades. Moroboshi refuses that premise and points to Toka as the third arrow. Civilian engineers, laborers, Self-Defense forces, knights and refugees restore the grid through the blizzard; Kanata shields repair crews and Kaieda coordinates the final transmission. Toka absorbs the entrusted electricity, breaks her death-chain vision through collective force, launches with Takemikazuchi, rejects Tendo's divine grace as unnecessary, and destroys God Breath and the storm-remnant with Raikiri. Kyushu's sky clears and Tendo dies realizing his Excessive Awakening was a delusion born from failing to rely on others. In the epilogue, Toka, Moroboshi and Kuraudo rest while Tokyo remains in a stalemate against Enterprise and a second U.S. wave. The command center then receives a shock report from Tsushima Base: Tsukikage is safe, and Ikki Kurogane is with him, undermining the U.S. war pretext and ending the volume on a reversal.
notes: Only character and event files were created per p1-scan instruction; ability/item/location/faction/system directories were not populated.
Chapter 7 is author afterword and was not used for in-world extraction.
Source chapter text labels itself 第十七卷 while path/task designate vol-19; output follows assigned volume path vol-19 and records the mismatch in volume_title.

The source split begins with an interlude and chapter four because earlier chapters are in the preceding assigned volume; extraction covers exactly the seven chapter files listed in vol-19/chapters.json.

Named supporting fighters and civilians were extracted when they materially affect the Daien operation, Tokyo defense, or final cliffhanger; unnamed repair crews, refugees, soldiers and operators are represented inside event summaries rather than separate character files.
The file characters/ito-family.json groups Mrs. Ito, her husband and son because their function in this volume is a small family/refugee perspective rather than sustained individual arcs.
